title: Giants beat Raiders as Featherstone see off Leigh
description: Huddersfield Giants beat Barrow Raiders while Featherstone Rovers see off Leigh Leopards in the Women's Super League.
fullText:
Huddersfield Giants maintained their good run against Barrow Raiders with a convincing 42-0 victory at a wet Craven Park in the Women's Super League.

Winger Mollie Iceton and full-back Amelia Brown scored two tries each in the first 40 minutes to put the Giants into a commanding 24-point lead at half-time.

Iceton completed her hat-trick and scored a fourth try in the second half before Samantha Hulme and Madison Clegg both went over as the Giants picked up a fifth consecutive win over the bottom-placed Raiders.

With just two matches of the regular season remaining, the Raiders are now staring down the barrel of a relegation play-off against the top-placed Championship team which are currently Swinton Lionesses.

Meanwhile, Featherstone Rovers comfortably beat Leigh Leopards 30-0 at Post Office Road.

Ellie Lamb broke the deadlock for the hosts before Aaliyah Brewster powered over underneath the sticks moments before the break.

Kate Evans extended Featherstone's lead in the second half and Cerys Gregory scored her first try for the club with less than 20 minutes remaining while Chloe Billington's late try put the seal on the win.

The victory means Rovers go four points clear of second-bottom Leopards and will face the Giants in the Shield Final.

title: Man Utd pay tribute to 'proud Red' officer who died in A66 crash
description: The widow and two children of PC Matthew Blades will be at Old Trafford for Manchester United's Premier League game with Ipswich.
fullText:
The two sons of a police officer killed in a crash on Teesside will lead out the Manchester United team as mascots for Sunday's Premier League match against Ipswich at Old Trafford.

PC Matthew Blades, described as a "proud Red" by United, was a regular at Old Trafford. The club have paid tribute to him in Sunday's match programme. His widow will attend the game with their children.

PC Blades and his colleague PC Tom Clough died in a head-on collision between their police car and a vehicle going the wrong way on the A66 near Middlesbrough early on 22 August. Five people in the other vehicle also died.

United said they learned of the deaths of the two officers "with great sadness".

"Matthew was a proud Red, a devoted family man and a police officer who dedicated his life to helping others," said the club, in a tribute in the programme.

At Elland Road, match officials for Leeds United's Premier League fixture against Brentford on Sunday wore black armbands as referee Tony Harrington was a friend of PC Blades.

On Saturday, there was a minute's applause in memory of PC Blades and PC Clough before Middlesbrough's Championship encounter with West Brom at Riverside Stadium. Pictures of the two men were displayed on a screen.

People also gathered to pay tribute at Seaton Carew FC's game against FC Hartlepool. PC Blades had been a junior football coach at both teams.

Earlier this week, 17 people were arrested in connection with the investigation into the crash bringing the total number of arrests to 24.

The occupants of the other vehicle, a Passat - Michael Robert Cahill, 23, Jacob Matusiak, 23, Makai Saddington, 18, Theo Rae, 17, and Cole Robert Worthy, 17, also died.

title: Pakistan to meet King Charles after Lord's controversy
description: Pakistan will have an audience with King Charles this week, days after a threat to cancel their tour of England was made because of an interview with the sons of Imran Khan.
fullText:
Pakistan will have an audience with King Charles this week, days after a threat to cancel their tour of England was made because of an interview with the sons of Imran Khan.

During lunch on day one of the second Test, Sky Sports aired an interview with Suleiman and Kasim Khan, the sons of former Pakistan captain and prime minister Imran.

Imran Khan has been in prison for the past three years on charges of corruption, which he denies.

Before the interview was aired, the Pakistan Cricket Board raised the prospect of not resuming the second Test at Lord's and cancelling the remainder of the three-match series.

At the time, the England and Wales Cricket Board took government advice from the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office.

Buckingham Palace has confirmed the King is expected to meet the tourists later this week in an engagement planned before the series began.

"His Majesty the King, as Head of the Commonwealth, will receive the Pakistan Men's Test Cricket Team for an audience in the gardens of Clarence House, in the break between the second and third Test matches hosted in England over the summer," said a statement.

It is understood His Majesty will spend around 15 minutes with the Pakistan team.

Legendary all-rounder Imran Khan, 73, had a 21-year international career for Pakistan and famously led his team to World Cup glory in 1992.

He served as Pakistan's prime minister from 2018 to 2022 and was jailed a year later.

Sarfaraz denies knowing about Pakistan threat to end tour

In December of last year, Imran Khan's sister appealed to King Charles in his position of head of the Commonwealth to speak out on the situation.

According to The Times, Aleema Khanum said: "Pakistan is a member of the Commonwealth of Nations.

"Its key principles in the charter are rule of law, democracy, and human rights. A member nation is busy destroying all three fundamental principles.

"Member states, especially where King Charles is the head of the Commonwealth organisation, don't speak out against fascism or military dictatorship? What is the point of just organisations then?"

The chairman of the PCB, Mohsin Naqvi, serves as interior minister for the current Pakistan government. The PCB has been contacted for confirmation Naqvi will be present for the audience with the King.

Before the interview with Khan's sons aired, Sky received a complaint, yet pressed ahead with airing a version of former England captain Michael Atherton's conversation with Suleiman and Kasim.

In the interview, Suleiman and Kasim expressed concerns over the treatment and security given to their father, as well as criticising the UK government's response.

Despite the controversy caused by the interview, the Pakistan team returned to the field as scheduled after lunch on the opening day of the second Test.

At the close of play on the second day, Pakistan coach Sarfaraz Ahmed said he and his team did not know about the interview.

"I don't know anything. I'm just focusing on the match," said Sarfaraz. "You're talking about the interview? We don't know about the interview."

In October, England will tour Pakistan for a one-day tri-series against the home side and Sri Lanka.

It will be England's fourth separate tour of Pakistan in the past four years following a 17-year gap between visits to the country because of security concerns.

title: Barcelona close to deal for Arsenal's Jesus
description: Barcelona are closing in on a move for Arsenal striker Gabriel Jesus in a deal worth £8.6m.
fullText:
Barcelona are closing in on a move for Arsenal striker Gabriel Jesus worth £8.6m (10m euros).

A deal for the Brazil international is believed to be at an advanced stage and, while the finer details still require finalising, the transfer is expected to be completed before Tuesday's deadline.

Napoli had shown an interest in Jesus, but the 29-year-old is set to join last season's Spanish league champions and will travel for a medical on Monday.

Jesus joined Arsenal from Manchester City in 2022, scoring 32 goals and adding 22 assists in 123 appearances for the Gunners.

Speaking to the media on Thursday, Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta confirmed that Jesus was not training with the squad before Monday's Premier League game against Aston Villa (20:00 BST).

When asked whether that meant Jesus was leaving, Arteta said: "Personal situations, whatever they are, I think it's clear."

Jesus would be Barcelona's third signing from a Premier League club this summer, following the arrivals of Anthony Gordon from Newcastle and Rodri from Manchester City.

Earlier this week, Barcelona's pursuit of Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alvarez - also an Arsenal target - appeared to end as sources told BBC Sport that Atletico would not negotiate with their Spanish rivals.

It looked as though Barcelona were not planning to sign another striker in the event of failing to capture Julian Alvarez from Atletico Madrid, who continue to make a deal extremely difficult.

However, the unexpected availability of Gabriel Jesus has changed Barca's approach. The Brazilian was not initially part of the club's plans, but the circumstances surrounding his situation at Arsenal have opened the door to a move.

Barcelona have taken advantage of the fact that he is no longer as prominent in Arsenal's squad as he has been, especially with Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyokeres now ahead of him in the pecking order.

With Jesus' Arsenal contract running until the summer of 2027, the club are willing to consider his departure for a fee rather than losing him on a free transfer next year.

The main question surrounding the move to Barca is Jesus' injury history. He has suffered significant knee problems during his time at Arsenal. An anterior cruciate ligament injury to his left knee, suffered in January 2025, kept him out for 10 months.

None of these necessarily means Barcelona will abandon their long-term interest in Alvarez.

Following Robert Lewandowski and Ferran Torres' departures from the club, Barcelona wanted to add a natural centre-forward to their attacking options. Jesus offers something different from a traditional number nine, with his ability to operate across the front line and contribute to the build-up making him an attractive option for Hansi Flick.

If the deal is completed, Flick will be adding a highly experienced forward to his squad. Jesus made 27 appearances for Arsenal last season in all competitions, scoring six goals, while his six-season spell at Manchester City produced 236 appearances and 95 goals.

For Barca, the move represents a relatively low-cost opportunity to add experience, versatility and Premier League pedigree to their attack.

title: 'These coaches are poison': Mohammad Yousuf calls out Babar Azam and Pakistan players' poor technique amid struggle in England
description: Former cricketer Mohammad Yousuf points out Babar Azam and his teammates' poor technique as Pakistan stare at another series defeat in England.
fullText:
'These coaches are poison': Mohammad Yousuf calls out Babar Azam and Pakistan players' poor technique amid struggle in England originally appeared on Cricket News. Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Mohammad Yousuf slammed coaches as Pakistan players get exposed in the England series.

England are on the verge of sealing the Test series at Lord's.

Yousuf raised questions on Babar Azam and his teammates' technique.

Pakistan's misfortune across all formats continues as they are on the verge of conceding yet another Test series against England.

The hosts are very close to sealing a series as they look to extend their lead over Pakistan to 400 runs in the second innings of the second Test at the iconic Lord's Cricket Ground.

Pakistan had earlier played a couple of Test series against Bangladesh and West Indies earlier this year. While they conceded a whitewash loss against Bangladesh, they somehow managed to hold West Indies to a 1-1 draw in their second away series of the year.

In England, Pakistan's performance thus far has been below and things got from bad to worst at the home of cricket as they were bowled out for just 110 runs in the first innings of the 2nd Test.

MORE: 'Not their fault': Mohammad Amir aims dig at current crop of Pakistan players as their struggle in England conditions continues

Former Pakistan batter and captain Mohammad Yousuf was critical of the current crop of Pakistan players as he raised questions on the playing technique of Babar Azam and Co.

On social media, Yousuf launched a scathing attack on the Pakistan players and also slammed the coaches who never bothered to correct the glaring mistakes in the players' playing style and technique.

On X, Yousuf wrote: "Few years ago I warned about this, but unfortunately some so called coaches around Babar Azam & other players didn't allow him to work on issues that could have been easily resolved. That failure has dragged Pakistan cricket into the decline we see today. These coaches are poison for the game. They lack vision, they block progress, and they misguide even the most talented players. If our cricketers don't learn who to listen to, their careers will end far sooner than they should. The poor technique of our players has now been brutally exposed from Bangladesh to England. What could have been corrected years ago has instead become a glaring weakness, leaving Pakistan cricket vulnerable and struggling on the international stage."

Few years ago I warned about this, but unfortunately some so called coaches around #Babarazam & other players didn’t allow him to work on issues that could have been easily resolved. That failure has dragged Pakistan cricket into the decline we see today.

These coaches are… pic.twitter.com/Go9kNc7abu

MORE: Cricketers speak out in support of Imran amid deteriorating health in jail

Pakistan's cricket standard has been falling for almost a decade now and their problems are deep-rooted. The nation which once produced legends of the game like Imran Khan, Zaheer Abbas, Wasim Akram and Waqar Younis, can no longer find world-class talents.

While Younus rightly pointed out that the coaches who have worked with the Pakistan team over the years should have worked closely with the players to improve their technique, it is also true that poor coaching is not the only reason for the poor standard of the national team.

It must be acknowledged that the Pakistan Cricket Board has failed to unearth quality talents in the country and their domestic cricket is practically a shambles. Unless the PCB improve the facilities and brings in structural changes, it is unlikely that Pakistan will recover from this mess they are in currently.

title: Sneak peak at Hornets’ new $190M training center, HQ
description: Playing for the Charlotte Hornets is about to get a whole lot better.
fullText:
Playing for the Charlotte Hornets is about to get a whole lot better.

On Aug. 28, team executives took reporters on a tour of the Hornets' $190 million training center, scheduled to open next spring — a project that leaves no doubt about the NBA franchise's willingness to invest in a winning product.

That theme resonated as Alex MacKenzie, the team's director of basketball facilities, led visiting media members through a maze of construction workers banging away on parts of the building.

At various stops inside the mostly completed shell of the 160,000-square-foot training and team headquarters — to be known as the Novant Health Performance Center — MacKenzie stood next to renderings displayed on easels and explained what the finished version will entail.

"We'll have a significant amount of the world's highest level of basketball technology in this space," MacKenzie said.

fullText:
Arsenal have announced they have completed the signing of Axel Donczew from Cardiff City.

The 16-year-old has joined the club as part of the first-year scholarship intake. He has also signed a pre-contract agreement that will lead to a professional deal when he turns 17.

Axel made headlines last October when he became Cardiff's youngest ever senior player.

He was only 15 years when he featured as a substitute in the EFL Trophy match against Newport County.

The Welsh youth international made his second first-team appearance for the Bluebirds last December against Wimbledon.

Axel mainly plays on the left wing but he can also operate as an attacking midfielder.

Arsenal have made several top additions to the squad this summer as they aim to defend their Premier League crown.

They have signed Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimaraes and Ezri Konsa from Club Brugge, Newcastle United and Aston Villa respectively.

The Gunners still seek a world-class forward and have firmly set their sights on Julian Alvarez.

Atletico Madrid have shown a willingness to consider an offer from the English champions. But Alvarez has already told manager Mikel Arteta he doesn't want to join Arsenal.

The Argentine could yet change his transfer stance, but a move to the Emirates Stadium looks unlikely with the summer window closing on September 1.

title: Richarlison in talks over shock Everton return – with Iliman Ndiaye moving other way to Tottenham
description: The forwards could trade clubs in separate deals as the end of the transfer window nears
fullText:
Tottenham and Everton are in talks about deals that could take Iliman Ndiaye to London and bring Richarlison back to Merseyside.

Spurs have targeted the Everton attacker as Roberto De Zerbi looks to complete the expensive overhaul of his forward line after they failed to score while losing their first two league games of the season.

Tottenham have brought in Savio for a minimum of £75m, which could rise to £85m, and Omar Marmoush, on a loan that will become a £60m purchase, from Manchester City.

Now they are looking to add Senegal international Ndiaye, who has scored 15 Premier League goals for Everton since his £15m move from Marseille two years ago. With the eventual transfer fee for Marmoush and buying Ndiaye, Tottenham's summer spending is set to go past £400m.

Manchester City also showed interest in the versatile Ndiaye, who has rejected multiple offers of a new contract from Everton, though they have made contact with Liverpool about signing Cody Gakpo instead.

While Everton have already done one swap deal this summer, signing Brennan Johnson from Crystal Palace while Dwight McNeil moved to Selhurst Park, these moves would come after separate conversations.

Richarlison was a popular player for Everton before his 2022 transfer to Tottenham, with the Merseyside club banking £60m when they were trying to avoid failing Financial Fair Play.

The Brazil international has scored 32 goals in 134 games for Tottenham after finding the net 53 times in his four years at Everton.

Everton could also lose teenager midfielder Harrison Armstrong, who is the subject of interest from Nottingham Forest, and manager David Moyes said after Saturday's 1-1 draw to Bournemouth that he did not want to sell anyone.

"I don't think we can afford to lose any players, certainly not our better ones," he said. "The club dictates a lot of that."

title: Cup night at the Volkspark! Fan info for BVB's game in Hamburg
description: Getting thereGetting there by trainAt the “Othmarschen” S-Bahn station (barrier-free), a free shuttle bus for away fans will be available from 6:30 pm, taking you close to the away entrance. You c...
fullText:
At the "Othmarschen" S-Bahn station (barrier-free), a free shuttle bus for away fans will be available from 6:30 pm, taking you close to the away entrance. You can reach Othmarschen from the main station on the S1 S-Bahn line (green line). The last return trip back to Othmarschen departs around 90 minutes after the final whistle.

The number of parking spaces around the Volksparkstadion is limited. Experience shows that the city and the motorway around the Elbe Tunnel are very busy during rush hour. It is therefore recommended to arrive as early as possible and allow plenty of extra time.

In general, the "Red," "Green," "Grey," and "Blue" car parks are available on matchday. Please note that the car parks—especially on the north side of the stadium—may also be used by home fans.

After leaving the motorway, please follow the signs to the Volksparkstadion and the parking guidance system. If you use a navigation system, please note that Uwe-Seeler-Allee is closed on matchdays.

Due to the closure of the "Brown" car park on Schnackenburgallee, this road must be avoided when accessing the "Red," "Grey," and "Blue" car parks.

The parking fee for cars is 10 euros.

The "Red" car park opens at 1:00 pm on matchday. All other car parks available at the stadium open at 4:30 pm.

Coaches park in the bus parking area on Schnackenburgallee. Access is via the HH-Volkspark motorway exit.

The car park opens at 4:30 pm on matchday.

The parking fee for coaches is 30 euros.

Due to the local conditions, delays when leaving the car parks after the match are to be expected.

The stadium opens two hours before kick-off, i.e. at 6:45 pm.

The away section is located in blocks 9 A/B/C to 14 A/B/C. Regardless of your block, all four entrances on the South Stand can be used. For material checks, the material entrance at the regular away entrance South/West must be used.

Away colours are not permitted anywhere in the North Stand.

Heavily intoxicated persons will not be admitted to the stadium.

Opposite the away entrance (South/West ramp) is Altona Cemetery. The HSV cemetery is part of this site. HSV asks away fans to treat this area with appropriate sensitivity, avoid leaving rubbish, and use the toilets on the stadium grounds.

To reach Luruper Chaussee, Stadionstraße should be used.

5 megaphones (already allocated)

Away fans with the "aG" designation may use the "Yellow" car park. Access runs from the "Yellow" car park towards the campus to the accessible ramp. Please note that due to capacity reasons, only stadium visitors who can show the "aG" designation on their ID may use this car park.

Accessible entry is via the wheelchair ramp at the South/East entrance. HSV helpers in red jackets are available to assist disabled fans around the Volksparkstadion and will also gladly accompany them to their seats. The platform for away fans in wheelchairs is located behind block 13 A. Seating for accompanying persons is available there.

Barrier-free access to the stadium

Bags and backpacks can be left free of charge in the immediate vicinity of the away entrance. Capacity is limited, however. Please avoid bringing them if possible.

Inside the stadium, payment can be made in cash, by card, or via mobile payment.

The clearing office is located at the South/East corner (ticket offices 19–24).

Please also note the applicable stadium regulations.

On Tuesday, fan liaison officers Justus Wadepohl (0160 99032215) and Marie Henke (0160 99238243), as well as Florian Hansing and Paul Brands from Fan-Projekt Dortmund e.V., will be available for you on site.

De Roon is a loyal supporter of the Grugliasco-born coach and is expected in the capital in the next few hours.

The Dutchman will replace Neil El Aynaoui, who is headed to Leipzig.

The 1991-born midfielder is ready to begin his adventure in the capital, but social media is unforgiving. Fans have resurfaced the player's old posts against the Giallorossi, and now it's up to him to make amends by letting the pitch do the talking.

title: COMMENTARY: Pressure's on Heupel as the season begins
description: Another 8-5 record ain't gonna cut it for Vol Nation
fullText:
Year No. 6 at Tennessee is going to be pivotal for coach Josh Heupel.

It was 2022, his second with the Volunteers, that Heupel enjoyed his best year with Hendon Hooker under center executing an offense that couldn't be stopped.

An injury to Hooker and a mind-numbing meltdown at South Carolina kept Tennessee out of the playoff.

Then came 2024. It was the Tennessee defense that paved the way for the Vols to be part of the first 12-team playoff, in spite of having to deal with Nico Iamaleava and his young mistakes at quarterback.

Last year's 8-5 season, with a defense that suffered a significant collapse late — especially against Vanderbilt — has left Heupel vulnerable to the pressure that coaches who have plenty of resources available to them feel when the results aren't there.

Not sure how another 8-5 would go over with the people in charge, let alone the Vol Nation fanbase.

I'm not suggesting that will be the case. I'm convinced that the Georgia Tech game in Week 2 will be quite important when it comes to getting this team ready for the rest of the season. That's when Faizon Brandon is convinced that he belongs under center and when the Vol defense realizes that coordinator Jim Knowles really does know what he's talking about.

Saturday against Furman will be just a dress rehearsal. Kennesaw State on Sept. 19 will be a time to work out the problems from Georgia Tech before Texas comes to town.

This is a time to trust Heupel. Give him the benefit of the doubt that he knows how to get a team ready for a season and navigate with a true freshman handling the football on every offensive snap.

What has impressed me the most about Heupel has been the way he deals with his players. He's honest. He isn't going to sugarcoat a situation. But, he's also not going to throw them under the bus.

Even the bad situations aren't going to be exacerbated by anything he said or did.

Take two very delicate situations he's handled in the past couple years. Both could have turned out a lot worse than they actually did.

The Iamaleava incident was a fiasco. After getting his team to the playoffs, Iamaleava and his entourage felt he was worth more than the reported $2 million annual NIL payment. He stopped showing up late in spring practice and tried to squeeze more out of Heupel.

Instead, Heupel let him walk and hit the jackpot with Joey Aguilar as a last-minute replacement.

Then there was Boo Carter. The talented sophomore defensive back and return specialist skipped a lot of the workouts in the summer of '25, and tried to get out of the doghouse in fall camp. The attempt lasted just a few games until Carter and the Vols parted ways.

Carter's family had a huge presence on social media but it didn't sway Heupel. Carter and his posse are Colorado's problem now. We'll see how Coach Prime handles it.

I'm convinced Heupel's still the guy for the Tennessee job. I've gone out on a limb saying this is a 10-2 playoff team.

Now, it's time to stop talking and start playing.

title: Phillies Castoff Nick Castellanos Takes Managing Role After Latest Cut
description: The Philadelphia Phillies received a surprising update on their former polarizing All-Star, who could be carving out a new career.
fullText:
The Philadelphia Phillies ended Nick Castellanos' tenure in dramatic fashion, cutting him shortly before the season began despite a significant remaining salary.

Castellanos had become a central figure in Philadelphia after signing a five-year, $100 million contract before the 2022 season. He produced 13 home runs and 62 RBIs during his first season with the Phillies and later helped the club reach the 2022 World Series.

But his relationship with the organization deteriorated. Reports surfaced that frustrations had grown between Castellanos and teammates and news surfaced that he had reportedly brought a beer into the dugout after being removed for defensive purposes in a game against the Miami Marlins.

"On the eve of Spring Training, the move came," AJ Cassavell reported for MLB.com. "Castellanos was released, entering the final year of his five-year deal with Philadelphia. The split was a messy one."

Since then, the Phillies have had to move forward with a different outfield mix while Castellanos moved on to the San Diego Padres. But that stint was short-lived, as he was released in June after failing to produce much at the plate.

Now it seems he has moved onto an entirely different type of role around the game.

Yankees Skipper Sends 3-Word George Lombard Jr Message Amid Record Error Streak

Now, a few months after his last at-bat, Castellanos announced that he will manage the Class of 2027 team at the 2026 All-American Game hosted by independent scouting service Prep Baseball.

"The 2026 event features an elite dugout lineup led by two-time MLB All-Star Nick Castellanos, who is managing the Class of 2027 team," Prep Baseball reported. "He's one of the few who knows what it's like to be in the shoes of these elite incoming seniors, having earned a famous reputation himself while thriving on the national circuit headed into his senior year, just before becoming the No. 44 overall pick in the 2010 Draft."

Castellanos' own reaction to the opportunity was characteristically brief.

"Marlins Park, talented kids," said Castellanos, according to the report. "I'm in."

While the decision to manage the game did not come with a formal announcement that his own playing days are over, it is a telling change for a former slugger who hasn't played much this season.

Former Braves Pitcher Punches, Pins Knife-Wielding Man To Protect Players, Per Report

The Phillies ultimately decided that their future was better served without Castellanos, creating an opportunity for other outfielders to take on larger roles.

For Castellanos, meanwhile, the All-American Game provides a chance to remain connected to baseball while passing along lessons from a 15-year major league career that included two All-Star selections and a World Series appearance.

It is not necessarily a sign that Castellanos has retired or abandoned hopes of returning to MLB. Instead, the coaching assignment gives him another way to stay involved in the game while showcasing the experience he accumulated as a highly regarded amateur prospect, first-round draft pick and established major league hitter, all in his native Miami.

This article was originally published on Forbes.com

title: Plaschke: No two ways about it — Shohei Ohtani should not pitch again this season
description: The Dodgers proved last season they need their two-way star to be an offensive catalyst and not a pitching sensation. They have the arms without him to win it all again.
fullText:
For a player who has been so improbable, the Dodgers must now do the impossible.

When it comes to pitching, they must shut Shohei Ohtani down.

Despite suffering a knee ailment and biceps soreness this season, Ohtani is slowly trying to take the mound for the first time in more than two months.

The Dodgers have no business sticking Ohtani back on the mound. He belongs out there no more than Kiké Hernandez does.

There's no two ways about it — the Dodgers should not plan on jamming Ohtani back into the starting rotation.

The Dodgers should thank him for his passion, applaud him for his 1.79 ERA in his first 14 starts, promise to return his resin bag next season, and ask him to go to work on that bat.

As much as the fans want to see all Ohtani, all of the time, the next couple of months are not about celebrating a novelty, they're about winning a championship, and Ohtani can best get that done by avoiding another injury to himself on the mound and directing all of his efforts at the plate.

Recently, his hitting needs all the help it can get. After Saturday's loss in Detroit, it had been a startling nine games since Ohtani homered or collected an RBI. During that span he had more than twice as many strikeouts as hits (13-5).

In this final month he needs to concentrate on getting his swing right and not worry about bullpens or openers or piggy-backs or any of the numerous machinations involved in getting him back on the mound.

Bottom line, the Dodgers need him more at the top of the order than in the middle of the diamond, and for now, he shouldn't be in two places at once.

Bottom, bottom line, there is a sense that the Dodgers agree.

Ohtani threw about 20 pitches in a bullpen session Friday and wasn't 100%, and that set off alarm bells with the Dodgers' bosses.

While guessing that Ohtani's balky left knee would not allow him to be 100% by October, manager Dave Roberts openly wondered Saturday whether a pitching comeback is worth the effort.

"Obviously, where we're at right now with the pitching, the starting pitching certainly being a strength, his value offensively is hugely important, and so we can't compromise that in any fashion," Roberts told reporters in Detroit. "So, if throwing potentially cuts into that, that's not worth the squeeze. So that's something for me. Very, very bullish on making sure we don't compromise the hitting."

Did you hear that? Not worth the squeeze? Exactly.

Are you listening, Ohtani? He's always been the ultimate team player, so if the Dodgers asked his permission to shut him down, he would agree, right? Right?

Keeping Ohtani off the mound for the rest of the season is a radical view, certainly — c'mon, you're paying the dude $700 million to hit and pitch! — but it's a view backed by common sense.

Point One: The Dodgers won a World Series in 2024 with Ohtani strictly hitting, so it can be done.

Point Two: Last postseason, even with his three-homer, 10-strikeout gem in the National League Championship Series against the Milwaukee Brewers, Ohtani had a playoff ERA of 4.43.

Playing in the postseason is hard. Pitching and hitting in the postseason is nearly impossible. That magical Brewers clincher was his only shining moment.

Point Three: They recently acquired Tarik Skubal specifically to reduce the need for Ohtani, and they now have a nearly unbeatable rotation without Ohtani.

With Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow having returned strong from injuries, they have four starters who easily can dominate a series.

Check out the current seven-game span of games started by Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Skubal, Snell and Tyler Glasnow.

They gave up as many as three runs only twice. They pitched less than six innings only once. Their ERA was 2.38.

Point Four: The struggling Dodgers offense desperately needs Ohtani to get right at the top. Who is going to get the big hit if he doesn't? Entering the last month, the candidates are few.

Not a slowing Mookie Betts. Not psyched-out Kyle Tucker. Not aging Teoscar Hernández. Maybe Freddie Freeman, but he hasn't hit a home run since July 4. And maybe Max Muncy, if they pitch to him.

Will Smith will be returning this week after a prolonged absence, and that will help, but not enough.

If anything happens to sideline Ohtani the hitter, the Dodgers are sunk, period.

And if he pitches, lots could happen to him.

The knee. The elbow. Whatever it was that has kept him off the mound since July 3. So much can go wrong if he's pitching, and any pitching injury could have the double whammy of sidelining him as a hitter.

"I think 100% for me as far as an offensive player, that's very important," Roberts said. "As a pitcher, for me, given the strength of our staff, our team, I don't think that's as important. I think it's important for us not to compromise his health in any capacity. But for me, it's just his presence in the batter's box is hugely important to him."

Yes, Ohtani wants to pitch. Yes, the Dodgers promised him he could pitch. But that was before the injuries and the acquisitions and the slump.

Everything is different now. The landscape has changed.

The Dodgers no longer need the arm so badly that they can risk the bat.

Barely 20 bullpen pitches at the end of August? He's clearly not going to be 100% by October, so shut him down and let him swing.

Shohei Ohtani is 32 and finishing his ninth season. He's not a kid anymore.

Having him pitch and hit for a second consecutive October indeed would be a great story.

But having him use his bat to lead the Dodgers to a three-peat would be a better one.

 Delivered at the start of each series.

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times.

title: Rory McIlroy predicts the score he needs to shoot in order to win the Tour Championship on Sunday
description: Rory McIlroy shot a scintillating 63 at East Lake on day three of the Tour Championship. McIlroy began his week slowly, shooting rounds of 68 and 69, so he desperately needed a low one on Saturday.
fullText:
Rory McIlroy shot a scintillating 63 at East Lake on day three of the Tour Championship.

McIlroy began his week slowly, shooting rounds of 68 and 69, so he desperately needed a low one on Saturday.

And that's exactly what happened.

Rory McIlroy was one-over par after two holes of his third round at the Tour Championship, but he followed that with nine birdies and one more bogey over his final 16 holes.

The six-time major champion's 63 hauled him back into contention, and he trails Viktor Hovland by five strokes heading into the final round.

McIlroy led the Tour Championship field in strokes gained putting on day three at East Lake.

And if he manages to take that form on the greens into Sunday, he will almost certainly have a chance to win.

McIlroy spoke to reporters after shooting a third-round 63 at East Lake on Saturday.

The Northern Irishman responded when asked how he feels about his position in the tournament with just 18 holes left to play.

"Yeah, I got myself back in the tournament," said McIlroy.

"We'll see what happens. We'll see how the leaders play the back nine. I feel like, if I'm within three or four of the lead going into tomorrow, we've seen what Cam did yesterday with a 62, goes out early. Bob did the same thing today with a 63, I shot a 63. There are scores out there.

"If I'm like a few groups before the leaders go out, maybe I can get off to a fast start and at least give them something to think about.

"It really depends on what the guys do this afternoon on the back nine. I would say, if I were to go out tomorrow and shoot the same score as I did today, I'd say that would have a very, very good chance."

McIlroy was speaking when Hovland was 13-under par.

Now that the Norwegian got to 15-under, the six-time major champion probably knows he will have to shoot even lower than 63 in order to stand a chance of winning.

McIlroy was asked what changed that enabled him to shoot a 63 after posting two fairly mediocre rounds to start his week at East Lake.

"Yeah, I think the difference today was I just putted a bit better. I putted a lot better," the Northern Irishman replied.

"I think I lost maybe a combined three shots on the greens over the first two days, and I probably gained over three on the greens today. So back to sort of even for the week.

"The ball striking has been there. I think I was second in ball striking to Gary Woodland the first couple days. It was another good display today. Hit some nice iron shots, drove it well for the most part.

"Look, it doesn't — I still felt like I played okay the last couple days, just wasn't getting as much out of my game as I wanted to. I pieced it together today and ended up obviously with a better score."

title: Hall of Famer survived Yankees owner George Steinbrenner: ’I'll never reclaim those years'
description: MLB legend Dave Winfield is hoping to inspire others to stand strong with his new book.
fullText:
New Yankees owner George Steinbrenner tried everything to break him and destroy his reputation to the point of no return, but Dave Winfield refused to let him win.

Winfield stood up to the most powerful owner in baseball, fought back just like he has throughout life, and now proudly tells his story with a book – and soon, a documentary.

It will not attract splashy headlines and have the internet buzzing. It won't make former teammates and managers uncomfortable with secrets that are unveiled. It instead provides a deep emotional dive into the man himself.

Winfield insisted from the start of the hour-long interview with USA TODAY Sports that for everyone who thinks they really know him, once you read "Touching All the Bases: A Story of Power, Purpose, and Surviving the Bronx," you'll find out that you really didn't know him.

Winfield poured his heart and soul into the book, which was nearly six years in the making, and will be released Sept. 15.

He talks about life as a Black athlete going against one of the most powerful men in sports in Steinbrenner, details the heartache and stress of court battles with a woman from his past, the pain of the George Floyd murder in Minneapolis across the river where he grew up in St. Paul, working in the players union and his frustration with former players who are part of commissioner Rob Manfred's ambassador program, performance-enhancing drugs, personal tragedy, his bout with prostate cancer, his philanthropic foundation, flying out of New York City the morning of the terrorist attacks and his heartbreaking trip to Ground Zero.

"I've had a unique life, legacy and experience, and I have a unique story to tell," Winfield says. "My life experience is so different than what most people would imagine. I'm in the seventh inning of life, so it's time to tell it.

"If you've got a unique experience or story, I believe you've got to share it with people."

The experience, as he details in his book: "My experience as a Black man who went to war with one of the most powerful owners in sports tells an essential story, not just about the triumphs and challenges of my own career, but about the dynamics of race and power in America."

Winfield, 74, isn't comparing himself to Jackie Robinson or Curt Flood, but no one else comes to mind in the past 50 years in baseball who was more tormented and mistreated, but courageously fought back, becoming a first-ballot Hall of Fame player and one of the most well-respected athletes in the sports world.

He survived Steinbrenner's attempts to bring ruin him, but in the end, it was Steinbrenner who went down, receiving a lifetime suspension that was reduced to 2 ½ years for hiring a gambler in a failed attempt to destroy Winfield's reputation.

"I could have been really vengeful, hateful, disrespectful, unhappy, for all of the things that were thrown at me," Winfield says. "But that never happened. I won't say I didn't have bruises and was bent a little bit, but I didn't break.

"When I think about my career, people will say was quite successful, but I don't really know how good I could have been at the pinnacle of my career if I had been supported. I think I would have been a better player."

It was when the world was shut down from COVID in 2020 that Winfield was home, watching the horrifying footage of George Floyd being strangled on the streets by a Minneapolis police officer, that he knew it was time to tell his story.

"I had something that George Floyd and so many other Black people didn't," Winfield writes, "a voice. A chance to speak, to be heard, and to defend myself. Too many people don't have that chance. I hope those coming up today keep the pressure on our leaders and stand alongside the 'old heads' who have fought through past struggles for equality.

"I hope they refuse to relent too soon and push tirelessly for real transformation."

Winfield can't wait now to meet and shake the hands of Kwanza Jones, who became the first Black majority owner of a baseball team when she and her husband, Jose E. Feliciano, purchased the San Diego Padres, his first team. It has been a long time coming, but finally, history was made.

"It would have been nice to see it sooner,'' Winfield says, "but it doesn't surprise me that it hasn't happened before now. I'm just happy it has happened now."

Winfield, who once was interested in being part of an ownership group himself, has plenty to share to whoever wants to listen. No other player in baseball history had such a highly publicized feud with his team owner, and lived to tell about it, with the owner being the one who was suspended from the game.

It was nasty. It was revolting. It was public.

"Those disputes weren't just about money," said Winfield, who signed a historic 10-year, $23 million contract with the Yankees, "they were about power. It was an owner, speaking for all the others, making sure a player knew his place."

Despite years without speaking after his departure, with Steinbrenner irate and canceling plans to retire his number after Winfield chose to wear a Padres cap cap into the Hall of Fame, Winfield's wife, Tonya, convinced him to see Steinbrenner perhaps for the final time. Winfield took a six-hour flight to Tampa in July 2008, two years before Steinbrenner died.

"I decided to make the trip," Winfield said, "hoping it might help quite some of the angry thought that had been pin-balling around my head for decades. …. When I saw him, it was clear he wasn't well. His handshake had weakened. He struggled for words and could barely speak above a whisper. I could see he didn't have the strength or clarity to have an in-depth conversation about our past."

They spoke for 90 minutes. It started with a handshake. It ended with a hug.

"Did the meeting give me a sense of reconciliation, closure, or validation?" Winfield said. "To some extent it did, but I'll never reclaim those years of anguish.''

Winfield, who spent 12 years as a special assistant in the players union before retiring last spring, is proud of playing a major role with the union. He has seen the union's power evolve from the first time he put on his first MLB uniform 53 years ago, going straight from the University of Minnesota to the big leagues with the Padres.

There was no free agency in 1973. No salary arbitration. The minimum salary was $16,000. Most players had second jobs in the winter.

Now, the average MLB salary is $5.34 million, with two players – Juan Soto and Shohei Ohtani – receiving free-agent contracts worth at least $700 million. Winfield made about $28 million his entire career, which is $32 million less than Dodgers right fielder Kyle Tucker is earning just this year.

"I expect the owners will do whatever necessary to get what they want," Winfield writes, "including fighting dirty and impugning reputations. I know from personal experience how dirty the fight can get. We must stand strong in defense of our hard-earned rights."

Winfield, the first of four Hall of Famers from his hometown of St. Paul – with Jack Morris, Paul Molitor and Joe Mauer – talks about being a proud Minnesotan, where he was honored in May with St. Paul erecting a statue of him in the Dunning Sports Complex. He played every sport growing up, and was drafted by four teams in three sports in 1973. The Padres selected him with the fourth pick in the draft, the fifth round by the Atlanta Hawks of the NBA and the sixth round by the Utah Stars in the ABA, and the Minnesota Vikings in the 17th round.

"Believe me, I tell many parents now to allow your kids to play other sports," Winfield said. "You're seeing these kids get injured or burnt out by playing one sport. Coaches want to dominate all of their time with one sport. Let them be kids."

Winfield, who begins his book tour on Sept. 8 with an appearance on "Good Morning America'' and "The View'' the following day, hopes that his book and an upcoming documentary will help inspire those facing their own adversity.

"I'm an outlier how you approach things in life,'' Winfield says. "I've never been afraid to travel, go outside, never afraid to meet new people. There are a lot of people that would roll up in a ball and quit if they faced all the negative stuff coming my way. I overcame really significant odds, ugly situations and a lot of adversity. I went through it all and came out Ok on the other end.

"Hopefully, people can be empowered, motivated and uplifted what I have written.''

Follow Nightengale on X: @Bnightengale

title: Lazio Keen to Sign Fringe Fiorentina Forward Who Is Open to the Move
description: Lazio are serious about recruiting Fiorentina forward Albert Gudmundsson, who finds himself on the periphery of the club’s project.The BackgroundThe 29-year-old is an Icelandic international who spe...
fullText:
Lazio are serious about recruiting Fiorentina forward Albert Gudmundsson, who finds himself on the periphery of the club's project.

The 29-year-old is an Icelandic international who spent his formative years in the Netherlands at Heerenveen and PSV Eindhoven. He also had a stint at AZ Alkmaar before moving to Genoa in 2021. The versatile attacker eventually became the Grifone's ultimate star, forming a deadly partnership with Mateo Retegui during th 2023/24 campaign.

Thanks to his exploits at the Luigi Ferraris, Gudmundsson was wanted by the biggest clubs in Serie A, but ended up joining Fiorentina in the summer of 2024 on a €17 million transfer. However, the skilful forward was never able to replicate his Genoa heroics in Florence. On Saturday, he was in the starting lineup as the Viola went on to suffer an embarrassing 0-3 defeat at home to Frosinone.

According to Italian journalist Alfredo Pedulla, Gudmundsson could be on his way out of Fiorentina, especially following the imminent arrival of Torino winger Alieu Njie. The transfer market expert reveals that Lazio have rekindled their old interest in the Icelandic player, contacting the Tuscan club to enquire about the costs of the operation.

Albert Gudmundsson (Photo by Gabriele Maltinti/Getty Images)

Pedulla adds that Lazio are 'very keen' to sign the 29-year-old, who is open to making the move to the Italian capital. The player is tied to Fiorentina with a contract valid until June 2029, and Transfermarkt estimates his value at €12 million.

Gudmundsson primarily features as a second striker (or an attacking midfielder), so his arrival would help Gennaro Gattuso switch to a 4-2-3-1 formation when needed. He is also capable of playing on the wings, particularly the left flank, as he can cut to the middle and shoot with his prolific right foot. Hence, he could vie for a starting role against Mattia Zaccagni in Lazio's current 4-3-3 system.

title: 'Don't make run scoring easier in Tests': Sunil Gavaskar rejects Sairaj Bahutule's free-hit in Tests suggestion to curb no-ball
description: Sunil Gavaskar rejected Sairaj Bahutule's free-hit proposal for Tests, urging escalating fines for bowlers and coaches instead.
fullText:
'Don't make run scoring easier in Tests': Sunil Gavaskar rejects Sairaj Bahutule's free-hit in Tests suggestion to curb no-ball originally appeared on Cricket News. Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Sunil Gavaskar wants fines for bowlers and bowling coaches after India's no-ball trouble during their Sri Lanka Test series win.

Ravindra Jadeja and debutant Saransh Jain repeatedly overstepped, with 13 no-balls bowled by India in the second Test alone.

Gavaskar dismissed bowling coach Sairaj Bahutule's idea of free hits in Tests, saying it would make batting even easier.

No-balls have become a bit of a headache for Team India, and Sunil Gavaskar isn't letting it slide quietly. Despite India's 1-0 series win over Sri Lanka, the former opener has pushed for fines, and plenty of them, for bowlers and bowling coaches every time someone oversteps the crease.

In just the second Test, India sent down 13 no-balls, with Saransh Jain and Ravindra Jadeja together responsible for 11 of those across both innings.

Jadeja's issues with front-foot no-balls aren't new, either, as he'd already leaked four in the series opener at Galle, which is now becoming a recurring theme throughout his career.

Since 2021, Jadeja alone has bowled more than 85 no-balls, which is a number that's hard to ignore for someone with his experience. Jain, playing his first Test, wasn't much better in the second innings at Colombo, spraying down several of his own.

MORE: 'Clueless captaincy': Furious fans and experts lash out at captain Gill

All this overstepping got India's bowling coach Sairaj Bahutule thinking out loud about whether Test cricket needs its own version of the free hit, borrowed straight from limited-overs cricket, to finally stamp out the problem.

Gavaskar wasn't having any of it and, writing in his Mid-Day column, he made his opinion pretty clear from the outset, as he argued that the no-ball issue needs sorting out fast before it starts swinging matches the wrong way.

"The no-balls being bowled by the Indian bowlers came in for a fair bit of comment. This has to be looked at urgently because it can change the colour of the game," he wrote.

He pointed out that overstepping is entirely avoidable these days, given how easy it now is to mark a run-up accurately. "There are very few aspects of the game that are totally in the players' control... today, with a tape measure available to mark the run-up, there should be no excuses for overstepping the bowling crease."

MORE: A series to remember for Sonal Dinusha: Yet another left-hander who has tormented India in Tests

As for the free-hit suggestion specifically, Gavaskar batted it away without much hesitation.

"The India team's spin coach jokingly said that giving a free hit after a no-ball might help in curbing the offence. Please, let's not make scoring runs in Test cricket easier for batters with this penalty," he wrote.

Rather than free hits, Gavaskar's pitching something with a bit more sting.

"How about a fine which gets doubled for every further transgression, plus half the amount of the fine for the bowling coach, too," he suggested, adding that the money collected could fund the team's farewell dinner at the end of a tour.

MORE: 'Don't think follow-on backfired': Gill defends decision to enforce follow-on

Honestly, Gavaskar's take here makes a lot more sense than Bahutule's off-the-cuff free-hit idea. Test cricket's already leaning batter-friendly; what with bouncer limits and shrinking boundaries and throwing free hits into the mix would just tip the scales further.

A no-ball in the longest format is a discipline issue, and bowlers have every tool available to avoid it. Escalating fines is smart precisely because it hits repeat offenders harder without messing with the actual contest between bat and ball.

Jadeja's numbers since 2021 tell their own story, as 85-plus no-balls isn't bad luck. It's a pattern that needed addressing years ago. If they start imposing fines, rather than handing free runs to the batting side, it keeps the focus where it belongs: on bowlers actually fixing a fixable problem, not on rewriting the format's balance to paper over it.

title: USA TODAY places Wisconsin's Luke Fickell on the "hottest" hot seat
description: Wisconsin Badgers head coach Luke Fickell enters the 2026 season with quite a but of pressure on his shoulders.
fullText:
Wisconsin Badgers head coach Luke Fickell enters the 2026 season with quite a bit of pressure on his shoulders.

In a new look at college football's hottest coaching seats, USA TODAY highlighted several coaches who need to make significant improvements this season, including Fickell.

UW's coach is entering his fourth season at Madison after the Badgers have struggled to find consistency under his leadership. Wisconsin finished with losing records in each of the last two seasons, making 2026 a particularly important year for Fickell and the program.

Fickell has previously acknowledged that he understands the pressure surrounding his position; now he needs to turn that pressure into positive results. Wisconsin has plenty of opportunities to make a statement this season, but the Badgers won't have much time to ease into the schedule as they open the year against Notre Dame before beginning Big Ten play.

Fickell arrived at Wisconsin with a strong reputation after guiding Cincinnati to an undefeated regular season and a College Football Playoff appearance. That success helped make him one of the most sought-after coaches when the Wisconsin job opened. However, three years later, the Badgers are still waiting to see that level of success in Madison.

The latest hot seat assessment is just another reminder that the pressure on Fickell isn't going away and that Wisconsin needs to win this year.

title: What New Mexico State head coach Tony Sanchez said after losing to FSU
description: The FSU Seminoles beat New Mexico State 34-17 on Saturday, here is what Tony Sanchez had to say about the game.
fullText:
The FSU Seminoles opened the season with a win over the New Mexico State Aggies, pulling out a 34-17 win in Doak Campbell Stadium. It was a much tougher game than expected, to the dismay of FSU's fans.

The Aggies were in the game from the start, driving on the field on the opening drive of the game before an interception ended the drive, allowing FSU to take an early lead. Despite the turnover, New Mexico State head coach Tony Sanchez liked what he saw from quarterback Trey Hedden.

"Yeah, I thought Trey really stepped up," he said. "We're big believers in him, and that's why we named him the starter. He's got some really good guys behind him, but I thought he did a really good job. They did a pretty good job of harassing him, and I thought the line stepped up too. I mean, I thought they played well.

"But he made one poor decision early on, on that interception. But other than that, I thought he played a really, really good game. He played a tough physical game. So I'm glad he's leading us."

Hedden completed 26 of his 42 passes for 272 yards and two touchdowns with the one interception. FSU was only able to sack him three times, with him doing a good job of getting the ball out quickly.

Sanchez also talked about the Aggies being fundamentally sound, his pride in them, and their struggles tackling FSU. Here is everything he had to say after FSU's win over New Mexico State.

Well, we got a good group of guys in that locker room. And I think the coaches did a really good job of driving these guys through camp.

We came in and we looked ready to play. I mean, that opening drive, seven minutes, just gotta be able to get some points out of it. It's tough when you hold the ball for seven minutes, move down the field kind of methodically.

And then you have an opportunity to go ahead and get a quick lead. You know what I'm saying? Turn it over. So that was disappointing, right? But again, I think we came out, we looked prepared to play the game.

Defensively, I thought the one Achilles heel we had all night was tackling in space. I thought our front did a pretty good job. I mean, they're a talented team.

They're gonna get some yards and things like that. But we gotta do a better job of shoring up the back end and being able to tackle back there. I thought that really, really hurt us.

So again, this game went on and we had our opportunities. It's a lot different when you're playing these money games and you walk in the locker room and there's some genuine disappointment that there was a great opportunity there. So I think we all own that, myself included.

We gotta do a better job of just tightening the screws and getting better at some of the little things, finishing second half. That opening drive, we have the ball again, we drive down. We don't end up completing that ball, and that should be another seven points right there, instead we kick a field goal.

Right after we score to make it a 10-point game, we get the personal foul. That's something that's a controllable. The things that are controllable, we have to own.

So I thought there were some really good things and there was a lot of great teaching moments. Again, no moral victory at all. I like our group.

I think if we do a good job as teachers, and they do a good job as students, I think that we'll continue to get better and move this thing forward.

There's no doubt, and I just think the culture of this group is solid. And part of that is them being together for a year. I talked to Coach Norvell before the game, and we both kind of reiterated the same thing.

We're having more fun doing this now than we have the last couple of years, because you know your guys, and your guys know you. And you have a chance to teach culture, teach discipline, hold on to some of those special guys. So like I said, I like the guys out there, and they had a good camp, and they came out, and they were ready to play tonight.

And unfortunately, we're walking out of here with a loss, and we're gonna have to knuckle up and go get back to 1-1 next week.

No, there's no doubt about it. I mean, we'll be back in the building tomorrow. We practice tomorrow night from six to seven o'clock. I expect it to be a fast, furious practice.

I expect us to get a lot of great things in. We have to have a great lift, great film session. We have to travel back like pros and get right back to work.

Yeah, I thought Trey really stepped up. We're big believers in him, and that's why we named him the starter.

He's got some really good guys behind him, but I thought he did a really good job. They did a pretty good job of harassing him, and I thought the line stepped up too. I mean, I thought they played well.

But he made one poor decision early on, on that interception. But other than that, I thought he played a really, really good game. He played a tough physical game. So I'm glad he's leading us.

Well, it's funny. When you're around a group of men like this, and you're in the building every day talking about, we fully expected to come win this game, and I think you saw that from the get-go. I mean, this was not a game we were coming in and be like, let's play well. I mean, we're disappointed.

We felt like we had a real opportunity to win a football game. So really disappointed in that. We did just a lot of things we need to work on.

We got to be more fundamental sound on the back end of our tackling. We got to sure of some special teams things. Offensively, we got to be able to run the ball with more efficiency than that.

That's pretty good defensive front. But I don't care who we are playing, we need to be a little bit more efficient running the football and continue to throw the ball down the field. So a lot of little things to get better at.

But excited to be back at Aggie Memorial playing in front of our home crowd. It should be a great environment. But if our kids continue to grow and continue to get better the way they did tonight, I think this could be a heck of a season, but we just gotta take it one game at a time.

So again, the goal this week, the only goal we have right now for this whole season, is to go 1-0 next week.

title: Mike Elko eyes 'winning plays' for Texas A&M in 2026
description: Mike Elko aims to fix Texas A&M's playoff woes by refining Marcel Reed's role and strengthening the defense, needing more "winning plays" this season.
fullText:
Playing "winning football" sounds vague on the surface, and heading into Mike Elko's third season at the helm, it's clear that the program is in the right direction, but back-to-back losses to Texas and Miami in the first round of the College Football Playoff were the antithesis of what we saw throughout the 2025 season.

This starts and ends with redshirt junior quarterback Marcel Reed, who threw four of his career-high twelve interceptions in both losses while seemingly playing with less confidence compared to his past performances, resulting in poor decision-making; former OC Collin Klein's decision to use fewer RPO looks and keep Reed in the pocket also deserves some blame.

Under first-year offensive coordinator Holmon Wiggins, the expectation is that Marcel Reed will return to utilizing his dual-threat skill set more often, getting outside the pocket, especially on play action where he has thrived since becoming the full-time starter. Equipped with one of the best wide receiver rooms in the country, Reed's improvement this preseason should lead to another jump in consistent play.

However, the defense allowed nearly 400 rushing yards against Texas and Miami last season, a huge contributing factor in both losses that wasn't based on personnel, aside from a lack of size at linebacker, which has been addressed this offseason.

During Thursday's press conference, Mike Elko said taking another step toward making "winning plays" in key moments has been a clear focus, starting with finishing strong every practice, while his team's mental makeup will be tested throughout the nine-game SEC schedule.

"We got to continue to be the team that steps up and makes those winning plays in those moments, and that's what we did in those games… That's what we didn't do in the playoff game."

"The more parity sets in, which it clearly is, and the more that the top comes down a little bit and the bottom comes up… It's going to come down to winning plays."

Situations where Marcel Reed is dropping back in 12 personnel and needing to make perfect throws in tight windows must be avoided, if possible, to avoid placing added pressure; this starts with a strong run game, which will open up play-action looks and allow the Aggies' wide receivers to make plays after the catch.

title: Tua Tagovailoa Breaks Silence After Harsh Fan Reception in Miami Return
description: Tua Tagovailoa returned to Miami Gardens with his new team Atlanta Falcons after spending six years here. Every return is special, but Tagovailoa’s return certainly wasn’t taken well by the home fans. After playing for Miami Dolphins for over half a decade, this was the first time he had played against the home team in […] The post Tua Tagovailoa Breaks Silence After Harsh Fan Reception in Miami Return appeared first on Gridiron Heroics.
fullText:
Tua Tagovailoa returned to Miami Gardens with his new team Atlanta Falcons after spending six years here. Every return is special, but Tagovailoa's return certainly wasn't taken well by the home fans.

After playing for Miami Dolphins for over half a decade, this was the first time he had played against the home team in Miami Gardens. As fans booed him loudly, he didn't pretend to not notice it, rather opened up about it after the game.

Despite spending years in Miami as the franchise quarterback, fans in attendance expressed their frustration. Many Dolphins supporters still felt let down by the team's lack of playoff success during his tenure as they achieved just one postseason appearance, alongside his turnovers and injury concerns toward the end of his run.

Despite the hostile reception, Tagovailoa took a reflective approach after the game. Addressing reporters, he acknowledged hearing the crowd but reiterated his lasting appreciation for the city and the team.

"Well, of course I did," Tagovailoa said. "But, you know, needless to say, like, being able to come back here, like, I've had six years here, and those are probably some of the best six years of my life, being able to, you know, play for Miami, being able to be in front of the crowd."

He tried to point toward the positives of the occasion. "You know, I mean, [I] had a Pro Bowl here, like, had a good amount of accolades. So, regardless of the reaction, like, I mean, I love the city. We have a home out here. Like, we still have our house and whatnot. But, I mean, it is what it is. You know, I can't change any of what they did and whatnot, but, you know, it was really cool to see a lot of the guys after the game, and then, you know, talk to some of the guys during the game. So it was a cool homecoming, if you will," he added.

Ignoring the harsh reception, Tagovailoa focused on his performance on the field completing 7 of 8 passes for 95 yards in a 17-12 Falcons win while treating his return as a positive opportunity to reconnect with former teammates. The hostile reception also drew a reaction from his former teammate Tyreek Hill who came to his defense online.

Tua Tagovailoa's signing with the Atlanta Falcons in March 2026 marked one of the most intriguing quarterback moves of the NFL offseason, signaling a fresh start for both the player and the franchise. Tagovailoa signed a one-year, veteran-minimum contract worth $1.215 million with Atlanta Falcons.

The transaction addressed an urgent need for Atlanta. With veteran Kirk Cousins departing during the 2026 free-agency period and third-year quarterback Michael Penix Jr. recovering from a knee injury sustained late in the previous season, the Falcons needed immediate stability and high-level depth under new head coach Kevin Stefanski.

Rather than handing out starting roles, the Falcons front office framed Tagovailoa's arrival as a true competition. Tagovailoa embraced the opportunity for a career reset, splitting first-team reps throughout training camp alongside a healthy Penix and veteran Cooper Rush.

title: Colts’ Anthony Richardson Makes His Case While Riley Leonard Falters in Preseason Finale
description: The Indianapolis Colts are set with their situation atop their quarterback depth chart. They will be led from under center in Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season by Daniel Jones, who has recovered from an Achilles injury he suffered last season in time for the upcoming campaign. Meanwhile, there still appears to be an […] The post Colts’ Anthony Richardson Makes His Case While Riley Leonard Falters in Preseason Finale appeared first on Gridiron Heroics.
fullText:
The Indianapolis Colts are set with their situation atop their quarterback depth chart. They will be led from under center in Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season by Daniel Jones, who has recovered from an Achilles injury he suffered last season in time for the upcoming campaign.

Meanwhile, there still appears to be an ongoing battle for the chief backup role behind Jones, with Anthony Richardson and Riley Leonard in the mix.

On Saturday, Richardson and Leonard each had a chance to further make their respective cases for the QB2 job during a real, competitive game, as the Colts faced the visiting Detroit Lions in a preseason finale at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis.

The former Florida Gators star quarterback Richardson started in that game, and he threw for 80 passing yards with zero touchdowns and no interceptions on 7/10 pass completions, while getting sacked for a loss of five yards.

Leonard, on the other hand, went just 3/7 for 48 passing yards with zero touchdowns and was intercepted deep in Lions territory.

Clearly, Richardson had the better outing than Leonard, so it will be interesting how that factors into Indianapolis' final decision on the QB depth order.

Indianapolis head coach Shane Steichen had good words for both Richardson and Leonard despite the latter giving away the ball when the team was on the cusp of scoring.

"I thought Anthony had some good drives, for sure," Steichen said, per the Associated Press (h/t ESPN).

"I think made some good throws, did some good things. I think Riley did some good things as well, just, obviously, don't want to turn it over there in the red zone. But I thought both of them did some good things."

The Colts ended up losing the game to the tune of 25-16 to conclude their preseason winless streak with a 0-2-1 record.

Indianapolis will open its season on Sept. 13 against the Baltimore Ravens at home.

fullText:
Liverpool view Cody Gakpo as a proven multi-functional Premier League attacker and he has shown that with a goal and an assist in their first two games this season.

But all summer, the understanding has been that if the club bring in the attacking players they want, they would not stand in the way of Gakpo if a solid offer came in.

Given how late in the transfer window the talks are taking place between Liverpool and Manchester City, the Anfield side will now consider the situation before sanctioning any move.

Liverpool are also hoping to bring in another winger before deadline day.

With the arrival of Victor Munoz, the emergence of Rio Ngumoha and Bradley Barcola's imminent move from PSG, Gakpo is well aware that he may not be first choice any more, so if a move does happen it would not come as a surprise.

Financially it will be a great outcome for Liverpool if they agree a deal for about £85m given they signed Gakpo for £35m from PSV Eindhoven after the World Cup in 2022.

But with Hugo Ekitike missing until 2027 with a ruptured Achilles tendon, and Alexander Isak's injury struggles, they would be taking a massive risk letting Gakpo leave.

title: Joe Mazzulla Gets Real on the ‘Burden and Love’ of Coaching the Celtics, Reveals Surprising Goal
description: Boston Celtics head coach Joe Mazzulla has always been known for having a different mentality. He isn’t the kind of coach who is focused on cementing his own name in NBA history.
fullText:
Boston Celtics head coach Joe Mazzulla has always been known for having a different mentality.

He isn't the kind of coach who is focused on cementing his own name in NBA history. Instead, his goal is centered around something far different from what most might expect.

Mazzulla has been at the helm in Boston since the 2022-23 season. Before taking over the Celtics, his only previous head-coaching experience came during a two-year stint at Fairmont State in West Virginia.

The Celtics coach has always carried an ambitious mindset, constantly looking for ways to take Boston to greater heights. However, his ultimate goal is not to build a legacy around his name or ensure he is remembered for everything he accomplished.

In an interview this week with Josh Chambers of the University of Maryland basketball program, Mazzulla revealed that his goal as the Celtics coach is, in fact, to be forgotten.

"If the people around you didn't do what they do," Mazzulla said. "I wouldn't do anything. The thing I reflect on the most is- I think you have to be willing to be forgotten. I think that's kind of my main goal."

"I want to be forgotten about. Because that means after you, it was better. I think that's what it means to be a Celtic. However long you play, coach, work for the Celtics."

Mazzulla has consistently rejected the idea of personal glory. For him, the true measure of his impact is whether the team is in a better position when his time at Boston ends.

"It's a burden and a love for being with the Celtics," Mazzulla continued. "But it's a responsibility. I think we could take that into our daily life. Can I leave it so much better that they don't remember me because the next person came and was better?"

Having guided the Celtics to their 18th NBA championship in 2024, Mazzulla has already accomplished something few coaches can boast of.

That championship also placed Mazzulla among the youngest coaches ever to win an NBA title. He became the ninth-youngest coach to accomplish the feat and the youngest since Bill Russell won a championship with Boston as a player-coach in 1969.

Following last season, Mazzulla added another major individual honor to his résumé when he was named NBA Coach of the Year, becoming just the fourth coach in franchise history to receive Coach of the Year honors.

title: Luka Doncic’s Style Harshly Judged By LeBron James’ 2016 Cavs Teammate, Says Lakers Star Will Stay Ringless Unless He Changes Game
description: The biggest criticism of Luka Doncic has been his defense. His former team reportedly pointed to it as one of the reasons they traded him. He believes Doncic will eventually win a championship, but he thinks the Los Angeles Lakers’ overall style of play could [...]
fullText:
The biggest criticism of Luka Doncic has been his defense. His former team reportedly pointed to it as one of the reasons they traded him.

However, a former NBA player-turned-analyst has a completely different observation. He believes Doncic will eventually win a championship, but he thinks the Los Angeles Lakers' overall style of play could prevent the Slovenian superstar from winning a ring.

Channing Frye, who was famously part of the 2016 Cleveland Cavaliers team that won the NBA championship led by LeBron James, believes Doncic's ball-dominant style and high usage rate will not lead his team to an elusive championship.

Doncic has already reached the NBA Finals once during his time with the Dallas Mavericks, although they lost to the Boston Celtics.

"I think Luka will win a championship," the retired NBA player said in his own podcast Channing's Mailbag.

"I do not think that he will win with that style of play and high usage rate. He needs a team around him, sure, but he plays physical and is usually beat up by the time. Did he miss his one chance? No. I just think something's going to come around where Luka got to come to grips with like, that's not what is going to win."

Frye's take is more about the team Doncic is playing for. He believes the Lakers should continue building around the six-time All-Star and add another player who can make Doncic trust the system and believe the team will be fine even when he is not dominating every possession.

The Lakers are already building around Doncic.

The superstar, who is coming off a long layoff that caused him to miss the 2026 postseason, reportedly had a wishlist of players, and the Lakers managed to acquire some of them.

He wanted a big man he could run the pick-and-roll with, and the Lakers signed Walker Kessler to a four-year, $130 million deal. He also reportedly badly wanted Austin Reaves back, and the Lakers rewarded the undrafted guard with a lucrative contract.

The Lakers also added Kevon Looney and Sandro Mamukelashvili to help Kessler in the frontcourt, Collin Sexton as a backup point guard, and Matisse Thybulle at the two-guard position.

There were also some major omissions from last season's starting lineup. LeBron James is now with the Philadelphia 76ers after deciding to become a free agent last June. Marcus Smart signed with the Houston Rockets, while Rui Hachimura signed with the Los Angeles Clippers. DeAndre Ayton was also traded to the Washington Wizards.

Doncic has been hands-on throughout the Lakers' summer preparations. He recently flew his team to Slovenia, where he hosted various workouts and team-building activities
